spans.title: The Walk on the Parapet
spans.blurb: A young woman steps onto a tower's narrow parapet to prove she can. The man watching her is not amused, until a slip changes the conversation entirely.
spans.spoilerNote: Shows Elfride warming to a second suitor, a courtship the novel develops gradually.

spans.title: Laocoön and the Serpents
spans.blurb: A priest sacrifices a steer at the shore when two great serpents come gliding over the sea, crests flaming, making straight for him and his young sons.

spans.title: A Splendid Hunting Ground
spans.blurb: A curious young mongoose scouts his splendid new garden, finds a nest of weeping birds, and hears a low cold hiss rise from the thick grass.

spans.title: The Council Rock
spans.blurb: On a moonlit hilltop, a wolf pack must decide whether a laughing man's cub may run with them, while a tiger roars for his prize in the dark.

books.pairNote: Two unrelated tales from the same collection, a mongoose vignette and a wolf-pack council; they coexist fine.

spans.title: The Word on the Wall
spans.blurb: At a murder scene, a proud detective unveils his prize discovery: a word scrawled on the wall in blood. An amateur with a tape measure reads it differently.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals the poison method and the revenge meaning of the bloody word, early deductions though not the killer's identity.

spans.title: The Hat Island Crossing
spans.blurb: A steamboat races the sunset toward a crossing no pilot dares run in the dark, while every man aboard stands watch in hand, silent.

spans.title: The First Train
spans.blurb: A young horse grazing by the railway meets a rushing, smoking black thing that shrieks and grinds past, and must decide how frightened to stay.

spans.title: The Night of the Broken Bridge
spans.blurb: Driving home through a wild autumn storm, a horse stops dead at the flooded wooden bridge and will not stir, whatever his master says.

books.pairNote: Two separate episodes from different points in the horse's life, with no shared text or payoff.

spans.title: The Shaving Glass
spans.blurb: A guest shaving at dawn is startled by his host's greeting; the mirror shows the whole room behind him, and no one else in it.
spans.spoilerNote: Tips early that the host is something inhuman, part of the novel's slow-building dread.

spans.title: The Derelict in the Storm
spans.blurb: A sudden tempest turns a glassy sea into a roaring monster, and watchers on the cliff spot a schooner, all sails set, driving straight for the harbour reef.

books.pairNote: A castle bedroom and a harbour storm, different narrators and settings with no shared reveal.

spans.title: The Man in the Wood
spans.blurb: A small boy waiting in a hallway shrieks and collapses in terror. What he points to, once he wakes, has been in the wall all along.
spans.spoilerNote: Links the child's terror to an ancient satyr-like presence, pointing toward the novella's central revelation.

spans.title: Dinner with an Old Bachelor
spans.blurb: Three genteel ladies dine at an old-fashioned farmhouse, where green peas defeat two-pronged forks and their host quotes poetry to the trees.

spans.title: A Vast Veil
spans.blurb: In a New England schoolhouse, children merrily trade visiting-cards until one glance of refusal shows a boy, all in a day, the world he stands outside.

spans.title: The School Behind the Hill
spans.blurb: A young teacher tramps the hot Tennessee hills hunting a school of his own, and finds one in a log hut behind a rail fence.
spans.brokenNote: The passage cuts off mid-sentence, ending on the dangling words "usually convinced them—for".

books.pairNote: Separate autobiographical episodes, one from childhood and one from young manhood, with no overlap.
